A1.justification: Both PDFs describe HD-Painter and retain the same central PAIntA, RASG, and super-resolution contributions. The complete text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support matching retained, revised, and removed content.

before.justification: v1 reports original MSCOCO evaluations, component ablations, a user study, qualitative comparisons, and appendix robustness experiments.

after.justification: v3 reports original quantitative comparisons, revised component ablations and user-study outcomes, and qualitative analyses in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The PAIntA transformation, RASG objective and sampling update, and two-stage super-resolution procedure remain unchanged. The backbone and eta changes concern experimental configurations; v3's newly specified first-half PAIntA schedule does not establish a change from an explicitly stated earlier schedule.

E1.justification: MSCOCO 2017 and the low- and high-resolution text-guided inpainting tasks remain. However, v1's targeted input conditions involving added positive/negative quality prompts and deliberate removal of an existing same-class object are no longer evaluated in v3. No new benchmark dataset or application domain is introduced.

E2.justification: The main comparisons remove NUWA-LIP and add SDXL Inpainting, DreamShaper Inpainting, DreamShaper-ControlNet Inpainting, and a SmartBrush reproduction. These methods participate in reported quantitative, qualitative, and user-study comparisons, substantially revising the comparator set rather than merely adding citations.

E3.justification: The evaluation backbone changes from Stable Inpainting 2.0 to DreamShaper 8, and the stated sampling parameter eta changes from 0.25 to 0.1. The user study reports 12 participants instead of 10, retaining 20 examples and the same two assessment questions. The 10,000-example MSCOCO setup and convex-hull masking remain.

E4.justification: v3 removes the positive/negative-prompt comparison, five-seed robustness tests, existing-object removal diagnostic, and dedicated combined-component visual ablation from v1 Appendices A, C, G, and H. PAIntA attention-map, guidance-strength, and objective-function analyses remain, with revised examples. This substantially reduces the range of diagnostic questions investigated.

E5.justification: v1 explicitly reports five randomly sampled seeds for the robustness comparisons in Figures 21–23; this repeated-generation evidence and run-count disclosure disappear in v3. Same-seed controls for component visualizations remain. Neither version reports confidence intervals or significance tests for the benchmark results.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces the reported HD-Painter CLIP/accuracy results of 26.34/61.4% with 26.25/67.59% under changed settings. Table 2 also changes the component ranking: combined accuracy was below RASG alone in v1 but exceeds both individual components in v3. Baseline scores, user-study votes, and many qualitative outputs change, while v1 Table 3 is removed. These are revised results, not controlled evidence of a between-version performance gain.

T1.justification: v3 corrects Equation (6)'s derivation of ordinary post-hoc guidance: the gradient contribution changes from plus to minus, and its coefficient is revised. Claim 1, the proposed RASG update, and the appendix derivations otherwise remain unchanged; no new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The training-free, prompt-aligned, up-to-2K contributions remain. However, v3 drops the introduction's explicit assertion that PAIntA and RASG can be added to any diffusion-based inpainting model, modestly narrowing the stated applicability. The abstract also replaces its specific accuracy headline with a general multi-metric and user-study superiority statement.

C2.justification: v3 adds an interpretation of SmartBrush's alignment-versus-image-quality tradeoff. It removes v1's explanations of existing-object suppression, complementary PAIntA/RASG failure modes, and quality-prompt tradeoffs. The limitations discussion also loses the concrete warning and mechanism explaining oversensitivity to unrelated positive prompt words, while retaining backbone-related anatomical failures.

D1.justification: v3 reports code as publicly available rather than promising a future release, supplies additional checkpoint access information, identifies the SmartBrush reproduction's DreamShaper basis, and specifies first-half PAIntA use. The exact positive/negative prompt lists disappear with their experiment. These are limited changes to reproducibility documentation.

R1.justification: v3 adds DreamShaper and SDXL references and removes references including NUWA-LIP, PAIR-Diffusion, Prompt-free Diffusion, and Versatile Diffusion. The introduction and Section 2.1 more explicitly credit SmartBrush and Imagen Editor with addressing prompt neglect through training and masking strategies, while retaining the paper's central training-free positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related-work discussion, and experimental narrative receive targeted rewrites. The user study moves from Appendix D into Section 4.1, aesthetic-score documentation moves into the main experimental setup, and the appendices are reorganized. Most method exposition and the conclusion remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: v3 transposes and expands the main and supplementary qualitative comparison grids, replaces many example panels, and widens Table 1 with additional methods and aesthetic scores. Figure 5 becomes a combined grouped user-study chart in the main text instead of two appendix plots. Several diagnostic figures are removed, while retained super-resolution comparisons and gradient histograms are relocated.

improvement.justification: The broader baseline comparisons and corrected Equation (6) strengthen v3, but the removal of seed-robustness tests, prompt-sensitivity evidence, and specific failure explanations weakens validation and transparency. Because the backbone and sampling settings also change, v3 supplies no replacement robustness evidence for its revised configuration. The net quality benefit of stronger comparative coverage versus these losses cannot be reliably established.
